articles.summary: 养鸡业希望把再生农业生产的鸡蛋发展成新的高端商品。这种农业改善土壤、减少环境影响，但能否让消费者理解并为可持续性支付更高价格，仍有分歧。

paragraphs.point: 从鸡在农场自由活动的场景引出气候友好鸡蛋，说明这些安排是有意设计的。
paragraphs.text: On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown's 40 windswept acres in Shiner, Texas. Some rest in the shade of a parked car. Others drink water with the cows. This all seems random, but it's by design, part of what the $ 6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-friendly eggs.

paragraphs.point: 解释再生农业如何改善土壤、留住温室气体，并成为产品卖点。
paragraphs.text: These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $ 8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they're also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture—special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases. Such eggs could be marketed as helping to fight climate change.

paragraphs.point: 用农场的作物、昆虫、鸡粪循环说明可持续系统如何运作。
paragraphs.text: “I'm excited about our progress,” says Brown, who harvests eggs for Denver- based Nest Fresh Eggs and is adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets for the chickens to eat. The birds' waste then fertilizes fields. Such improvements “allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed that will be good for the land, the hens, and the eggs that we supply to our customers.”

paragraphs.point: 用有机鸡蛋等产品从小众到主流的经历说明市场潜力。
paragraphs.text: The egg industry's push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering. In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart. More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories. If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.

paragraphs.text: Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine. articles.summary: 越来越多美国人选择退休后继续工作，这既与寿命延长、经济准备有关，也与保持思维活跃、获得个人满足感有关。文章最后提醒，退休需要同时做好财务与心理准备。

paragraphs.text: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade. Even more surprising is that more than half of “unretirees”—those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring—said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.

paragraphs.point: 区分经济原因和精神原因：保持头脑活跃、避免无聊或抑郁。
paragraphs.text: Financial needs aren't the only culprit for the “unretirement” trend. Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression. About 72% of “unretiree” respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.

paragraphs.point: 概括退休观念正在变化，工作自身也能提供价值。
paragraphs.text: “The concept of retirement is evolving,” said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade. “It's not just about finances. The value of work is also driving folks to continue working past retirement.”

paragraphs.point: 用人口寿命和老年就业的数据说明变化背景。
paragraphs.text: One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer. The share of the population 65 and older was 16% in 2018, up 32% from the prior year, according to the US. Census Bureau. That's also up 302% since 2010. Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the US. workforce, and boomers are expected to live longer than previous generations. The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades. About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.

paragraphs.point: 说明人们如何通过减少支出等方式增加储蓄。
paragraphs.text: Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, the TD Ameritrade study showed, which surveyed 2000 adults between 40 to 79. Six in 10 “unretirees” are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life, according to the survey. Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts.

articles.title: 识别并约束诱导用户的暗黑设计
articles.summary: 文章解释利用界面设计操控用户决定的“暗黑模式”，指出企业各团队和监管者都应参与治理，而企业自律和问责是持续避免欺骗设计的关键。

paragraphs.point: 用容易注册却难以取消的服务引出暗黑模式，说明它损害自主选择。
paragraphs.text: We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives. Think about the times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless sign-up process but was later difficult to cancel. Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice. These are examples of dark patterns.

paragraphs.point: 介绍术语来源和典型类型，例如诱导、隐藏费用和难以退出。
paragraphs.text: First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, “ dark patterns” is a catch-all term for practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users. Brignull identifies 12 types of common dark patterns, ranging from misdirection and hidden costs to “roach motel,” where a user experience seems easy and intuitive at the start, but turns difficult when the user tries to get out.

paragraphs.point: 研究说明这类设计相当普遍，企业应认识其灰色地带。
paragraphs.text: In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one in 10 employs these design practices. Though widely prevalent, the concept of dark patterns is still not well understood. Business and nonprofit leaders should be aware of dark patterns and try to avoid the gray areas they engender.

paragraphs.point: 建议跨部门审查，区分合理说服与数字欺骗。
paragraphs.text: Where is the line between ethical, persuasive design and dark patterns? Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy policy, and include in the discussion the customer/user experience designers and coders responsible for the company's user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets, pricing, and promotions. Any or all these teams can play a role in creating or avoiding “digital deception.”

paragraphs.point: 介绍加州法规，要求用户能够清楚行使隐私权和退出选择。
paragraphs.text: Lawmakers and regulators are slowly starting to address the ambiguity around dark patterns, most recently at the state level. In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that “ensure that consumers will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights.” The regulations aim to ban dark patterns—this means prohibiting companies from using confusing language or unnecessary steps such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn't opt out.”

paragraphs.point: 强调企业应对法律、行业实践和标准承担责任，不能只等监管。
paragraphs.text: As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, there is a need for greater accountability from within the business community. Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable, not just to legal requirements but also to industry best practices and standards.

articles.title: 一堂伦理课能改变吃肉行为吗
articles.summary: 一项真实校园研究发现，讨论肉食伦理的学生随后购买含肉餐食的比例下降。研究者承认效果原因和持久性尚不确定，社会影响、情感和理性论证都可能参与其中。

paragraphs.point: 提出伦理课能否改变行为的问题，并介绍新研究的积极发现。
paragraphs.text: Although ethics classes are common around the world, scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports. But a new study published in Cognition found that, in at least one real-world situation, a single ethics lesson may have had lasting effects.

paragraphs.point: 交代研究设计：比较肉食伦理讨论组与慈善讨论组，观察匿名餐卡记录。
paragraphs.text: The researchers investigated one class session's impact on eating meat. They chose this particular behavior for three reasons, according to study co-author Eric Schwitzgebel, a philosopher at the University of California, Riverside: students' attitudes on the topic are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good because it reduces environmental harm and animal suffering. Half of the students in four large philosophy classes read an article on the ethics of factory-farmed meat, optionally watched an 11-minute video on the topic and joined a 50-minute discussion. The other half focused on charitable giving instead. Then, unknown to the students, the researchers studied their anonymized meal-card purchases for that semester—nearly 14,000 receipts for almost 500 students.

paragraphs.point: 呈现与原先预期相反的结果：前者肉食购买比例下降且持续数周。
paragraphs.text: Schwitzgebel predicted the intervention would have no effect; he had previously found that ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books. But among student subjects who discussed meat ethics, meal purchases containing meat decreased from 52 to 45 percent—and this effect held steady for the study's duration of several weeks. Purchases from the other group remained at 52 percent.

paragraphs.point: 其他研究者指出可能存在未控制因素，效果也可能逆转。
paragraphs.text: “That's actually a pretty large effect for a pretty small intervention,” Schwitzgebel says. Psychologist Nina Strohminger at the University of Pennsylvania, who was not involved in the study, says she wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable. And if real, she notes, it might be reversible by another nudge: “Easy come, easy go.”

paragraphs.point: 讨论社会、情感和理性等可能机制，并以研究者改变看法收尾。
paragraphs.text: Schwitzgebel suspects the greatest impact came from social influence- classmates or teaching assistants leading the discussions may have shared their own vegetarianism, showing it as achievable or more common. Second, the video may have had an emotional impact. Least rousing, he thinks, was rational argument, although his co-authors say reason might play a bigger role. Now the researchers are probing the specific effects of teaching style, teaching assistants' eating habits and students' video exposure. Meanwhile, Schwitzgebel—who had predicted no effect—will be eating his words.

articles.title: 中断之后怎样重新开始锻炼
articles.summary: 文章给出安全恢复锻炼的办法：从较小强度开始，注意身体反馈，保持规律，先练习动作，并利用同伴支持提高坚持的可能性。

paragraphs.point: 开头解释恢复运动不容易，活动量过多过快可能造成损伤或身心疲惫。
paragraphs.text: Getting back into exercise can be a challenge in the best of times, but with gyms and in-person exercise classes off-limits to many people these days, it can be tricky to know where to start. And it's important to get the right dose of activity. “Too much too soon either results in injury or burnout,” says Mary Yoke, PhD, a faculty member in the kinesiology department at Indiana University in Bloomington. The following simple strategies will help you return to exercise safely after a break.

paragraphs.point: 先降低距离、频率、重量，再逐步提高，不能期望一夜恢复。
paragraphs.text: Don't try to go back to what you were doing before your break. If you were walking 3 miles a day, playing 18 holes of golf three times a week, or lifting 10-pound dumbbells for three sets of 10 reps, reduce activity to half a mile every other day, or nine holes of golf once a week with short walks on other days, or use 5-pound dumbbells for one set of 10 reps. Increase time, distance, and intensity gradually. “This isn't something you can do overnight,” says Keri L. Denay, MD, lead author of a recent American College of Sports Medicine advisory that encourages Americans to not overlook the benefits of activity during the pandemic. But you will reap benefits such as less anxiety and improve sleep right away.

paragraphs.point: 根据呼吸和疲劳调整运动量，严重不适应及时就医。
paragraphs.text: If you're breathing too hard to talk in complete sentences, back off. If you feel good, go a little longer or faster. Feeling wiped out after a session? Go easier next time. And stay alert to serious symptoms, such as chest pain or pressure, severe shortness of breath or dizziness, or faintness, and seek medical attention immediately.

paragraphs.point: 强调规律性，从每天短时间步行开始培养习惯。
paragraphs.text: Consistency is the key to getting stronger and building endurance and stamina. Ten minutes of activity per day is a good start, says Marcus Jackovitz, DPT, a physical therapist at the University of Miami Hospital. All the experts we spoke with highly recommend walking because ifs the easiest, most accessible form of exercise. Althoughit can be a workout on its own, if your goal is to get back to Zumba classes, tennis, cycling, or any other activity, walking is also a great first step.

paragraphs.point: 暂时不能正式运动时，也可模仿动作，唤起乐趣并准备肌肉。
paragraphs.text: Even if you can't yet do a favorite activity, you can practice the moves. With or without a club or racket, swing like you're hitting the ball. Paddle like you're in a kayak or canoe. Mimic your favorite swimming strokes. The action will remind you of the joy the activity brought you and prime your muscles for when you can get out there again.

paragraphs.point: 与他人一起或借助线上方式锻炼，获得督促与乐趣。
paragraphs.text: Exercising with others “ can keep you accountable and make it more fun, so you're more likely to do it again,” Jackovitz says. You can do activities such as golf and tennis or take a walk with others and still be socially distant. But when you can't connect in person, consider using technology. Chat on the phone with a friend while you walk around your neighborhood. FaceTime with a relative as you strength train or stretch at home. You can also join a livestream or on-demand exercise class.

articles.logic: 总述恢复运动的难点→循序渐进→关注反馈→养成习惯→练习动作→借助同伴。小标题要概括整段建议。

pitfalls.explanation: dose 借用剂量概念，不是指服药。
此处要求根据身体反应减量，不是彻底放弃运动。

pitfalls.meaning: 让你受到督促、更愿意坚持
pitfalls.explanation: accountable 不是会计或记账。

articles.title: 画作失控也能带来成长
articles.summary: 绘画成果不如预期并不一定是坏事，意外结果可以训练人应对失望、调整方法和创造性解决问题，而这些能力也有助于日常生活。

paragraphs.point: 说明光线、材料、经验和技巧会让作品偏离原计划。
paragraphs.text: Although we try our best, sometimes our paintings rarely turn out as originally planned. Changes in the light, the limitations of your painting materials, and the lack of experience and technique mean that what you start out trying to achieve may not come to life the way that you expected.

paragraphs.point: 把意外结果转化为成长机会：学会应对失望、适应变化并想出新办法。
paragraphs.text: Although this can be frustrating and disappointing, it turns out that this can actually be good for you. Unexpected results have two benefits: you pretty quickly learn to deal with disappointment, and realise that when one door closes, another opens. You also quickly learn to adapt and come up with creative solutions to the problems the painting presents, and thinking outside the box will become your second nature.

paragraphs.point: 将绘画中培养的创造性问题解决能力推广到日常生活。
paragraphs.text: In fact, creative problem-solving skills are incredibly useful in daily life, with which you're more likely to be able to find a solution when a problem arises.

articles.logic: 预期受挫→解释两种收获→迁移到生活。

pitfalls.meaning: 真正呈现出来、成为现实
pitfalls.explanation: 指构想成为画面，不是死而复生。
不是走到盒子外面。

pitfalls.meaning: 习以为常、自然具备的能力
pitfalls.explanation: 表示经过练习后变得自然而然。

articles.title: 跨部门增长团队如何推动业务
articles.summary: 文章用软件公司的经历说明，跨部门协作能够发现单一部门看不到的增长障碍；增长团队还需要明确目标、善于协调并帮助团队保持专注的领导者。

paragraphs.point: 提出小企业发展遇到的共同问题，并介绍增长团队的跨部门性质。
paragraphs.text: Here's a common scenario that any number of entrepreneurs face today: you're the CEO of a small business and though you're making a nice 1, you need to find a way to take it to the next level. what you need to do is 2 growth by establishing a growth team. A growth team is made up of members from different departments within your company, and it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus 3 on finding ways to grow.

paragraphs.point: 以软件公司增长停滞为例：免费用户多，付费升级却少。
paragraphs.text: Let's look at a real-world 4. Prior to forming a growth team, the software company BitTorrent had 50 employees. Working in the 5 departments of engineering, marketing and product development. This brought them good results until 2012, when their growth plateaued. The 6 was that too many customers were using the basic, free version of their product. And 7 improvements to the premium, paid version, few people were making the upgrade.

paragraphs.point: 新经理组建团队，用营销视角发现问题在于用户不了解付费版。
paragraphs.text: Things changed, 8, when an innovative project marketing manager came aboard, 9 a growth team and sparked the kind of 10 perspective they needed. By looking at engineering issues from a marketing point of view, it became clear that the 11 of upgrades wasn't due to a quality issue. Most customers were simply unaware of the premium version and what it offered.

paragraphs.point: 营销与工程部门合作提高产品知晓度，带来升级和收入增长。
paragraphs.text: Armed with this 12, the marketing and engineering teams joined forces to raise awareness by prominently 13 the premium version to users of the free version. 14, upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent.

paragraphs.point: 从个案转向一般建议：增长团队需要强有力的领导者。
paragraphs.text: But in order for your growth, team to succeed, it needs to a have a strong leader. It needs someone who can 15 the interdisciplinary team and keep them on course for improvement.

paragraphs.point: 说明领导职责：确定方向、目标与期限，排除偏离目标的想法。
paragraphs.text: This leader will 16 the target area, set clear goals and establish a time frame for the 17 of these goals. This growth leader is also 18 for keeping the team focus on moving forward and steer them clear of distractions. 19 attractive, new ideas can be distracting, the team leader must recognize when these ideas don't 20 the current goal and need to be put on the back burner.

articles.logic: 提出增长问题→讲述案例及转机→总结团队领导的职责。

pitfalls.explanation: plateau 作动词，不是地形上的高原。
用上船的比喻表示到任。
不是把想法放在炉灶上。

articles.title: 人造草坪的环保争议
articles.summary: 园艺组织认为塑料草坪损害环境并限制其使用，支持者则强调天然草坪同样消耗资源。政府暂不全面禁止，而是要求遵守现有生态保护规定，反映出这一产品的持续争议。

paragraphs.point: 从塑料草坪流行及花展禁用引出其环境与生物多样性问题。
paragraphs.text: In the quest for the perfect lawns, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut -- and it is the environment that is paying the price. About eight million square meters of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles. The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year's event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos. The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.

paragraphs.point: 园艺组织说明为什么支持真草，并列举生态好处。
paragraphs.text: Ed Horne of the RHS said: we launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic. We recommend using real grass because of its environment benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment.

paragraphs.point: 环保倡议者通过社交账号和请愿推动禁售及征税。
paragraphs.text: The RHS's decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problem fake grass causes. A Twitter account, which claims to “cut through the greenwash” of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers. It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an “ecological damage” tax on such lawns. They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures.

paragraphs.point: 行业反驳：天然草坪也消耗水、电力、燃油和药剂，人造草坪可伴随其他园林种植。
paragraphs.text: However, supporters of fake grass point out that there's also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol. The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more. The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend on average of £500 trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects.

paragraphs.point: 政府回应此前请愿，表示暂无全面禁止计划。
paragraphs.text: In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has "no plans to ban the use of artificial grass.

paragraphs.point: 政府倾向引导选择、执行现有法规和生态保护义务。
paragraphs.text: It added:"We prefer to help people and organizations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters, However the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives."

articles.logic: 争议背景→反对理由与行动→行业辩护→政府立场；作者呈现双方论据，不能把行业声称直接视为已证实事实。

pitfalls.explanation: 此处付出代价的是环境，不是仅指购买价格。

pitfalls.meaning: 把产品包装成环保的宣传
pitfalls.explanation: 这里的账号声称揭露人造草坪的环保包装。
lay 在这里不是下蛋。

articles.title: 国家公园需要稳定的公共投入
articles.summary: 文章承认美国国家公园资金短缺、设施失修，但反对把营地商业化视为根本解决办法。公园具有公共、文化和生态价值，需要增加而不是削弱公共财政支持。

paragraphs.point: 用夸张的商业场景质疑政府拟议的创收办法。
paragraphs.text: It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks. Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?

paragraphs.point: 承认问题真实存在：大量维护工程积压、基础设施老化。
paragraphs.text: But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.

paragraphs.point: 指出营地只是问题的一小部分，商业经营上缴收入有限。
paragraphs.text: But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all. Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.

paragraphs.point: 进一步论证商业化会破坏游客逃离日常商业喧嚣的体验。
paragraphs.text: Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.

paragraphs.point: 把问题根源归于长期资金不足，并以调查说明公众愿意多付税款。
paragraphs.text: The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding. An economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.

paragraphs.point: 列举公园在自然、教育、气候、文化和历史保护方面的广泛价值。
paragraphs.text: The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature. On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism. The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life.

paragraphs.point: 对比长期不增长的拨款与不断增加的游客数，强调投入不足。
paragraphs.text: The parks do all this on a shoestring. Congress allocates only 3 billion a year to the national park system — an amount that has been flat since 2001 ( in inflation-adusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009. Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.

articles.logic: 质疑方案→承认危机→说明方案不足及副作用→提出资金根源→证明公共价值→用预算与需求对比收束。

pitfalls.explanation: backlog 指未处理事项的累积，不是已经偿还的债务。

pitfalls.meaning: 无处不在、反复出现的商业宣传
pitfalls.explanation: 鼓点是比喻，强调日常生活里持续的商业干扰。
不是鞋带上的动作。

pitfalls.meaning: 剔除通胀后基本没有增加
pitfalls.explanation: 不能只看名义金额不变或把 flat 译成平坦。

articles.title: 互联网改变记忆的内容还是能力
articles.summary: 研究发现，人们在知道信息可以再次查询时，更倾向于记住去哪里找信息，而不记住信息本身。这可能是适应新工具而非记忆能力衰退，但互联网对大脑的总体影响尚需研究。

paragraphs.point: 通过实验区分记住信息本身与记住信息位置，提出记忆正在适应新技术。
paragraphs.text: The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow. In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer ("an ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain," for example). Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved. Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers. In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders. In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but "adapting to new communications technology," Sparrow says.

paragraphs.point: 解释认知卸载：借助外部存储，把学习重心转向概念理解。
paragraphs.text: In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as "cognitive offloading." Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans. Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance. Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society but Sparrow sees an upside. Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking - something that is not available on the Internet. “I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things," Sparrow says, adding that we haven't lost our ability to do it.

paragraphs.point: 其他研究者提醒证据不足，并给出上网可能锻炼大脑的研究。
paragraphs.text: Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains. There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons. And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.

paragraphs.point: 承认成本和收益并存，对记忆改变是否更好保持谨慎。
paragraphs.text: "There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I'd have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs," observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm. "It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don't know."

articles.logic: 实验发现→概念及潜在好处→证据边界→审慎结论；重点区分记忆内容变化与记忆能力下降。

pitfalls.meaning: 把一部分记忆任务交给外部工具
pitfalls.explanation: 例如记住文件夹位置而非全部信息，不等于失去记忆能力。
用作互联网帮助记忆的比喻，drive 不是驱动力。
末段的 observe 是引出观点，并非观察实验对象。

articles.title: 青春期的叛逆与助人倾向为何并存
articles.summary: 研究表明，青少年不仅叛逆和冒险行为增强，助人等亲社会行为也会增强，两者还呈正相关。对社交奖励更加敏感可能是它们共同的发展因素。

paragraphs.point: 提出青春期的矛盾：独立和互助增长的同时，顺从儿童也会变成叛逆者。
paragraphs.text: Teenagers are paradoxical. That's a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language. But the paradox is scientific as well as personal. In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other. At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers.

paragraphs.point: 介绍新研究视角：青春期既有风险，也是机会。
paragraphs.text: A new study published in the journal Child Development by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand. The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence. For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem needed to be solved. The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk.

paragraphs.point: 交代研究如何调查助人和叛逆行为。
paragraphs.text: The researchers studied "prosocial" and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old. The participants filled out questions about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late.

paragraphs.point: 两类行为都呈现青春期上升、之后下降的相似模式。
paragraphs.text: Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increased as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older. But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior. Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly help a friend.

paragraphs.point: 进一步指出叛逆越强的青少年也越可能帮助他人。
paragraphs.text: Most significantly, there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness. The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others. The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together.

paragraphs.point: 提出共同解释：对奖励的敏感度影响风险和收益权衡。
paragraphs.text: Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments? One idea is that teenager behavior is related to what researchers call” reward sensitivity." Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs “Reward sensitivity” 'measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk.

paragraphs.point: 说明青少年尤其看重社交认可，并用成年后的变化作对照。
paragraphs.text: Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards-winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you. Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age. Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn't seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.

articles.logic: 提出矛盾→介绍研究→呈现两类行为的共同变化→寻找共同心理机制。正相关不表示叛逆直接造成助人。

pitfalls.meaning: 冷静客观、不带强烈感情的
pitfalls.explanation: 描述作者对青春期的温和说法，不是人与人完全分离。

pitfalls.meaning: 有利于他人或社会的、亲社会的
pitfalls.explanation: 指帮助朋友等行为，不仅是善于社交。
指对回报的反应强度，文章尤其讨论社交认可。

articles.title: 节能建筑新规的短期成本与长期收益
articles.summary: 英国提高住宅节能标准，会增加房屋扩建改造的初期费用，也限制部分空间和玻璃面积；长期看更节能舒适，并可能通过能源账单节省收回成本。

paragraphs.point: 提出新规将提高新建、扩建和阁楼改造费用。
paragraphs.text: New building regulations aimed at improving energy efficiency are set to increase the price of new homes, as well as those of extensions and loft conversions on existing ones.

paragraphs.point: 交代政策目标及通风、保温、供暖和充电设施要求。
paragraphs.text: The rules, which came into effect on Wednesday in England, are part of government plans to reduce the UK's carbon emissions to net zero by 2050. They set new standards for ventilation, energy efficiency and heating, and state that new residential buildings must have charging points for electric vehicles.

paragraphs.point: 行业指出材料与人工已涨价，新规将进一步增加支出。
paragraphs.text: The moves are the most significant change to building regulations in years, and industry experts say they will inevitably lead to higher prices at a time when a shortage of materials and high labour costs is already driving up bills.

paragraphs.point: 建筑业代表解释新材料、测试和系统安装带来的成本。
paragraphs.text: Brian Berry, chief executive of the Federation of Master Builders, a trade group for small and medium-sized builders, says the measures will require new materials, testing methods, products and systems to be installed. “All this comes at an increased cost during a time when prices are already sky high. Inevitably, consumers will have to pay more,” he says.

paragraphs.point: 测量师强调扩建和改造房主会直接受影响。
paragraphs.text: Gareth Belsham, of surveyors Naismiths, says people who are upgrading, or extending their home, will be directly affected.

paragraphs.point: 具体指出保温、窗门和玻璃使用量的要求。
paragraphs.text: “The biggest changes relate to heating and insulation,” he says. “There are new rules concerning the amount of glazing used in extensions, and any new windows or doors must be highly insulated.”

paragraphs.point: 估计普通扩建工程可能增加约三千英镑。
paragraphs.text: The changes could mean an extra £3,000 added to the bill of an average home extension, according to Jonathan Rolande of the National Association of Property Buyers, a group of professionals aimed at raising construction standards.

paragraphs.point: 更厚的墙体可能使可用室内面积变小。
paragraphs.text: Homeowners extending may see the amount of space they have decrease, as walls will have to be thicker in order to comply with requirements for better insulation.

paragraphs.point: 建筑师给出外墙需要加厚的具体幅度。
paragraphs.text: Andrew Mellor, of PRP architects, says external walls will need to be about 7cm thicker than previously.

paragraphs.point: 更高门窗标准和玻璃面积限制用于减少热量问题。
paragraphs.text: Windows and doors will have to adhere to higher standards, while there are new limits on the amount of glazing you can have to reduce unwanted heat from the sun.

paragraphs.point: 报价服务人士说明扩建也会受到限制。
paragraphs.text: Thomas Goodman, of My Job Quote, a site which sources quotes, says this will bring in new restrictions for extensions.

paragraphs.point: 给出玻璃面积不超过地板面积四分之一的要求。
paragraphs.text: “Glazing on windows, doors and roof lights must cover no more than 25% of the floor area to prevent heat loss, ” he says.

paragraphs.point: 密闭性提高后，需要微型通风口保证空气流通。
paragraphs.text: As properties become more airtight, there are also measures to ensure proper airflow, such as having small openings (trickle vents) on windows that allow ventilation when a window is closed.

paragraphs.point: 供暖系统可能需要改变，并加强管道保温。
paragraphs.text: For people extending their homes, they may be required to install a new, or replacement, heating system depending on the size of the build, says Belsham. These will have to use lower temperature water to deliver the same heat, which will require increased insulation of pipes.

paragraphs.point: 说明保温与通风需兼顾，避免过热和冷凝积聚。
paragraphs.text: “We'll see more insulation, better lighting design and restrictions on the amount of glass used in some areas. But with more thermal-efficient homes can come the risk of overheating due to solar gain, and so ventilation is also covered,” says Rolande. “As a result, double-glazed windows will require trickle vents to let heat escape and also to provide fresh air for health reasons and, of course, to reduce the risk of condensation build up in an ever-more airtight property.”

paragraphs.point: 开发商赶在生效前提交计划，争取适用旧规则。
paragraphs.text: As the rules came into effect last Wednesday, property developers were rushing to file plans just before the deadline, according to Belsham. Any plans submitted before that date are considered to be under the previous rules, and can go ahead as long as work starts before 15 June next year.

paragraphs.point: 原文重复摘出普通扩建可能增加约三千英镑这一估计。
paragraphs.text: An average extension will probably see around £3,000 additional cost thanks to the new regs

paragraphs.point: 尚未提交文件的建筑商可能要重新估价。
paragraphs.text: Builders which have costed projects, but have not filed the paperwork, may need to go back and submit fresh estimates, says Marcus Jefford of Build Aviator, which prices projects.

paragraphs.point: 概括长期节省供暖费与短期施工费提高的对比。
paragraphs.text: As the changes are aimed to make homes more energy efficient, they will eventually drive down heating bills. But in the short-term homeowners are likely to face higher costs for work.

paragraphs.point: 以材料价格上涨数据补充成本背景。
paragraphs.text: Materials prices are already up 25% in the last two years, according to figures from the Construction Products Association.

paragraphs.point: 指出总涨幅尚不清楚，已有买房困难者会面临更多压力。
paragraphs.text: How much overall prices will increase as a result of the rule changes is not clear. “While admirable in their intentions, they will add to the cost of housebuilding at a time when many already feel that they are priced out of homeownership,” says Rolande. “An average extension will probably see around £3,000 additional cost thanks to the new regs.”

paragraphs.point: 律师预计技术普及后价格会下降，但眼下需承担转型成本。
paragraphs.text: John Kelly, a construction lawyer at Freeths law firm, believes prices will eventually come down. But not in the immediate future. “As the marketplace adapts to the new requirements, and the technologies that support them, the scaling up of these technologies will eventually bring costs down, but in the short term, we will all have to pay the price of the necessary transition,” he says.

paragraphs.point: 建筑师强调长期舒适节能，并有望逐渐收回成本。
paragraphs.text: However, the long-term effects of the changes will be more comfortable and energy-efficient homes, adds Mellor. “Homeowners will probably recoup that cost over time in energy bill savings. It will obviously be very volatile at the moment, but they will have that benefit over time.”

articles.logic: 新规目标→具体施工影响→估算与过渡安排→短期成本和长期收益对比。

pitfalls.explanation: extension 不是电话分机；conversion 不是货币兑换。

pitfalls.explanation: 文章关心门窗与屋顶玻璃所占面积及保温性能。
不是引用语。

articles.title: 诗歌怎样让语言鲜活起来
articles.summary: 文章从华兹华斯与浪漫主义引出诗歌的感染力，再说明诗歌早于文字出现，兼具叙事和传承历史的作用；朗诵可以让节奏与声音更清晰，也促进理解。

paragraphs.point: 以华兹华斯和浪漫主义对自然的赞美引入诗歌。
paragraphs.text: In the late 18th century, William Wordsworth became famous for his poems about nature. And he was one of the founders of a movement called Romanticism, which celebrated the wonders of the natural world.

paragraphs.point: 说明精心选择的语言、节奏和意象能打动读者。
paragraphs.text: Poetry is powerful. Its energy and rhythm can capture a reader, transport them to another world and make them see things differently. Through carefully selected words and phrases, poems can be dramatic, funny, beautiful, moving and inspiring.

paragraphs.point: 回顾诗歌与故事、历史和歌曲的联系，并强调朗诵有助于感受与理解。
paragraphs.text: No one knows for sure when poetry began but it has been around for thousands of years, even before people could write. It was a way to tell stories and pass down history. It is closely related to song and even when written it is usually created to be performed out loud. Poems really come to life when they are recited. This can also help with understanding them too, because the rhythm and sounds of the words become clearer.

articles.logic: 代表人物→艺术感染力→历史功能与阅读方式。

pitfalls.explanation: celebrate 在这里并非举办庆祝活动。
不是把人捕获或抓起来。
指朗诵把诗的声音与节奏展现出来。

articles.title: 为社交找到合适的节奏
articles.summary: 社交不足和社交过度都可能让人状态变差。文章建议识别自己的需求，通过兴趣活动建立联系，同时为休息和恢复留出时间。

paragraphs.point: 定义社交生活并指出个体差异：有些人社交后充满能量，有些人会耗竭。
paragraphs.text: Your social life is defined as 'the activities you do with other people, for pleasure, when you are not working'. It's important to have a social life, but what's right for one person won't be right for another. Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, 1 some of us may feel drained, even if it's doing something we enjoy.

paragraphs.point: 说明孤独可能影响心理健康，居家办公和人生转变也会带来孤独。
paragraphs.text: This is why finding a 2 in your social life is key. Spending too much time on your own, not 3 others, can make you feel lonely and 4. Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and 5 a low mood. Anyone can feel lonely at any time. This might be especially true if, 6 you are working from home and you are 7 on the social conversations that happen in an office. Other life changes also 8 periods of loneliness too, such as retirement, changing jobs or becoming a parent.

paragraphs.point: 建议从兴趣出发寻找群体，逐步建立社交联系。
paragraphs.text: It's important to recognise these feelings of loneliness. There are ways to 9 a social life. But it be overwhelming 10. It's a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy. You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet 11 people. There are groups aimed at new parents, at those who want to 12 a new sport for the first time or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and 13 ideas.

paragraphs.point: 提醒社交过量也会造成耗竭，识别信号并安排恢复时间。
paragraphs.text: On the other hand, it is 14 possible to have too much of a social life. If you feel like you're always doing something and there is never any 15 in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social 16. We all have our own social limit and it's important to recognise when you're feeling like it's all too much. Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be 17 of poor social health. Make sure you 18 some time in your diary when you're 19 for socialising and use this time to relax, 20 and recover.

articles.logic: 个体差异→社交不足的风险→建立联系的方法→社交过多的风险与界限。

pitfalls.explanation: 不是身体失水。
不是只指机器停机。
这里用来安排时间，不是写私人感想。

articles.title: 人工智能的收益需要更广泛地分享
articles.summary: 文章担忧，人工智能收益过度集中于少数城市和精英，会加剧不平等并削弱公众支持。解决方向是扩大独立和区域研究投入，并把人工智能用于创造当地真正需要的机会。

paragraphs.point: 提出AI与不平等的关系，引用经济学家强调进步收益需要更公平分享。
paragraphs.text: Anger over AI's role in exacerbating inequality could endanger the technology's future. In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress. “Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past,” she writes. “An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable.”

paragraphs.point: 说明提高生产率需要数字技术，但公众要感受到实际好处才会接受变化。
paragraphs.text: Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle. But people can't be expected to embrace the changes if they're not seeing the benefits—if they're just seeing good jobs being destroyed.

paragraphs.point: 指出技术转型需要社会认同，不平等可能成为部署AI的障碍。
paragraphs.text: In a recent interview with MIT Technology Review, Coyle said she fears that tech's inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI. “We're talking about disruption,” she says. “These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed.” To make such “tremendous changes,” she adds, you need social buy-in.

paragraphs.point: 对照理想与现实：不少人因收益流向少数精英而产生不满。
paragraphs.text: Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities.

paragraphs.point: 用就业和AI资源集中的城市数据说明地域分布不均。
paragraphs.text: According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019. New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings's Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States (San Francisco and San Jose alone account for about one-quarter).

paragraphs.point: 说明集中化会加剧地区财富差距和社会动荡，反过来妨碍技术发展。
paragraphs.text: The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar. Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow.

paragraphs.point: 提出增加独立研究及区域创新中心投入，减弱大科技公司的议程控制。
paragraphs.text: Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda. That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants. Muro and others have suggested hefty federal funding to help create US regional innovation centers, for example.

paragraphs.point: 提出更直接的方向：想象能扩展各地区重要行业机会的AI，而非只替代岗位。
paragraphs.text: A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don't simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.

articles.logic: 分配问题→社会接受前提→集中化证据→社会及技术后果→研究投入与应用方向的解决方案。

pitfalls.explanation: buy-in 是认同，不是购买技术设备。

pitfalls.expression: a stranglehold on the AI agenda
pitfalls.meaning: 对AI发展议程的强力控制
pitfalls.explanation: 是控制权的比喻，而非真实扼住喉咙。
末段要求重想AI的应用方向，不只是为既有AI项目筹钱。

notes: 原题库第6、7段在同一句中硬断行；理解时合并为一段。

articles.title: 增加木材林种植以应对未来建造需求
articles.summary: 英国木材供应高度依赖进口，长期忽视本土木材生产可能引发建造材料短缺。林业组织希望政府在生态保护之外，也重视生产性植树，提供落实目标所需的支持。

paragraphs.point: 提出未来建造危机，说明本土木材供应少、进口依赖高。
paragraphs.text: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned. The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country's reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations. Currently only 20 percent of the UK's wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world.

paragraphs.point: 认为现有植树激励不足，长期投资不足使英国暴露于价格波动和供给竞争。
paragraphs.text: Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don't go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies. “Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of failure to plant trees to produce wood.” said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor. "For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall."

paragraphs.point: 说明英国具备可持续木材生产条件，并对比苏格兰与英格兰。
paragraphs.text: The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says. While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 percent.

paragraphs.point: 肯定食物生产和生物多样性，同时要求重视木材林的经济和减碳作用。
paragraphs.text: While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK's net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity. Goodall add： “ While food production and biodiversity are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net zero.

paragraphs.point: 指出口头植树目标尚缺落实，呼吁增强行动推动力。
paragraphs.text: “While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground." Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand."

articles.logic: 供给危机→政策及投资不足→本土生产条件→兼顾多重土地用途→要求落实。

pitfalls.explanation: 不是交易身体。
与仅为生物多样性种植原生林相对照。
ground 表示实际工作层面，不仅指土地表面。

articles.title: 让老年人安全驾驶需要协调与适老设计
articles.summary: 老年人停止开车会面临生活方式的大变化，医生报告义务与隐私规定又因地区而异。文章主张协调研究、改善评估与就医条件，并发展适合高龄驾驶者的车辆，而非寄希望于自动驾驶包办解决。

paragraphs.point: 说明劝说不安全的老年驾驶者交出车钥匙很难，停驾会改变生活。
paragraphs.text: One big challenge in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it is time to turn over the key. It is a complete life-changer when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke.

paragraphs.point: 介绍医学建议及各州不同的报告、保密和责任规定。
paragraphs.text: The American Medical Association advises physicians that in situation where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician's advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles, Menke wrote. “Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report breach of confidentiality. There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality ” she counseled.

paragraphs.point: 指出现有各专业分别处理问题，缺乏协调和充分证据。
paragraphs.text: Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan. “There's not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies,” she said. “We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe” and what can help, said Dugan.

paragraphs.point: 研究显示当面换证和视力检查与致命事故下降有关。
paragraphs.text: One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal. Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study. Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two.

paragraphs.point: 先说明医疗跟进、记忆和驾驶设置等现实困难，再指出自动驾驶并非万能，应设计适合高龄者的车辆。
paragraphs.text: Many old drivers don't see eye doctors or can't afford to. Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can't turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven't changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily, As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won't solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan. Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require to many algorithms, she said. But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan. “If we're going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably.”

articles.logic: 现实阻力→职业和法律约束→协调不足→评估措施→现实障碍与适老设计。

pitfalls.explanation: 不是泛指车辆损坏。
在这一语境是驾驶许可，而非财富带来的优待。
形容基层医疗人员难以再承担充分随访。

notes: 原题库倒数第二段以逗号结束，前端会与最后一段接在一起；这里按当前显示的五个自然段组织提示。

articles.title: 健康应用的数据保护存在空白
articles.summary: 健康应用广泛收集个人信息，但既有医疗隐私法律并未同等覆盖这些数据。文章用企业分享敏感信息的案例说明风险，指出联邦执法往往只能事后介入，而州级立法正在补足保护。

paragraphs.point: 用健康应用数量和类型说明其普及程度。
paragraphs.text: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several. Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form. Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.

paragraphs.point: 对比传统医疗信息保护与健康应用、可穿戴设备数据保护之间的缺口。
paragraphs.text: While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online. Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors ' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online. The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections.

paragraphs.point: 以Flo Health事件说明未经明确同意分享敏感数据的风险和整改要求。
paragraphs.text: Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated. In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission（FTC） investigation. The FTC alleged in a complaint that "despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users' sensitivity fertility data and shared it with third parties.” Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users' express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.

paragraphs.point: 解释联邦贸易委员会的事后执法权限及应对新应用迅速增加的困难。
paragraphs.text: Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company's privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm. While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.

paragraphs.point: 认为短期联邦全面立法前景有限，介绍多个州的立法行动。
paragraphs.text: As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia ， Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.

articles.logic: 普及→法律覆盖空白→个案→执法边界→州级补救。

pitfalls.explanation: express 是形容词，不是表达某种感情的动词。
强调监管常在问题发生后介入。

pitfalls.meaning: 利用健康信息获取收益
pitfalls.explanation: 不一定只是直接卖出数据，也包括其他盈利使用。

articles.title: 大学申请中的课外活动重在质量
articles.summary: 招生专家认为，大学申请中的课外活动不应只追求数量；持续投入、突出的个人能力、与未来专业的联系及对社区的贡献，更能帮助学生展示独特价值。

paragraphs.point: 从学生为申请选择大量课外活动的常见现象切入。
paragraphs.text: High school students eager to stand out in the college application process often participate in a litany of extracurricular activities hoping to bolster their chances of admission a selective undergraduate institution.

paragraphs.point: 提出总论点：活动质量比数量更重要。
paragraphs.text: However, college admissions experts say that the quality of a college hopeful's extracurricular activities matter more than the number of activities he or she participates in.

paragraphs.point: 专家说明通用申请表不必填满十项。
paragraphs.text: Sue Rexford, the director of college guidance at the Charles. E. Smith Jewish Day School, says it is not necessary for a student, filling out the Common Application to list 10 activities in the application

paragraphs.point: 进一步解释大学不会期待学生对大量活动都长期深入投入。
paragraphs.text: “No” college will expect that a student has a huge laundry list of extracurricular that they have been passionately involved in each for an tended period of time, " Rexford wrote in an email.

paragraphs.point: 指出在普遍参与的活动中脱颖而出更难。
paragraphs.text: Experts say it is tougher to distinguish oneself in a school-affiliated extracurricular activity that is common among high school students than it is to stand out while doing an uncommon activity.

paragraphs.point: 建议参与热门活动时力求做得突出。
paragraphs.text: “The competition to stand out and make an impact is going to be much stiffer, and so if they're going to do a popular activity, I'd say, be the best at it.” says Sara Harherson, a college admission consultant.

paragraphs.point: 独立完成、令人印象深刻的个人项目也有价值。
paragraphs.text: High school students who have an impressive personal project they are working on independently often impress colleges, experts say.

paragraphs.point: 用创办盈利小企业举例说明创业兴趣与能力如何展示。
paragraphs.text: “For example, a student with an interest in entrepreneurship could demonstrate skills and potential by starting a profitable small business.” Olivia Valdes, the founder of Zen Admissions consulting firm, wrote in an email.

paragraphs.point: 说明不常见活动可以体现独特性，但必须有真正投入。
paragraphs.text: Joseph Adegboyega-Edun, a Maryland High school guidance counselor, says unconventional, extracurricular activities can help students, impress college admissions offices, assuming they demonstrated, serious commitment. “Again, since one of the big questions high school seniors must consider is 'What makes you unique? ' having an uncommon, extracurricular activity, a conventional one is an advantage,” he wrote in an email.

paragraphs.point: 在至少一项活动中展示才能有利于申请。
paragraphs.text: Experts say demonstrating talent in at least one extracurricular activity can help in the college admissions process, especially at top-tier undergraduate institutions.

paragraphs.point: 解释顶尖院校希望看到成绩之外的特质及其对校园的贡献。
paragraphs.text: “Distinguishing yourself in one focused type of extracurricular activity can be a positive in the admissions process, especially for highly selective institutions, where having top grades and test scores is not enough,” Katie Kelley admissions counselor at Ivy Wise admissions consultancy, wrote in an email. “Students need to have that quality or hook that will appeal to admissions officers and allow them to visualize how the student might come and enrich their campus community.”

paragraphs.point: 活动若与未来主修专业相关，可形成额外优势。
paragraphs.text: Extracurricular activities related to the college major declared on a college application are beneficial, experts suggest. “If you already know your major, having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus,” says Mayghin Levine, the manager of educational opportunities with The Cabbage Patch Settlement House, a Louisville, Kentucky, nonprofit community center.

paragraphs.point: 积极影响社区的活动可能帮助申请和奖学金评定。
paragraphs.text: High school students who have had a strong positive influence on their community through an extracurricular activity may impress a college and win a scholarship, says Erica Gwyn, a former math and science magnet program assistant at a public high school who is now executive director of the Kaleidoscope Careers Academy in Atlanta, a nonprofit organization.

articles.logic: 质量优于数量的总原则→热门与独特活动的选择→个人专长→专业关联→社区贡献。匹配题要对应每位专家的独特主张。

pitfalls.explanation: 不是洗衣清单，指堆砌活动数量。

pitfalls.meaning: 能打动招生官的独特亮点
pitfalls.explanation: 此处不是鱼钩，也不是取巧手段。

articles.title: 农贸市场连接食物、生产者和社区
articles.summary: 农贸市场既提供丰富的感官体验，也让顾客了解食物来源、支持本地经济；减少中间环节可以让农民得到更多收益，顾客也更清楚钱流向谁。

paragraphs.point: 通过气味、色彩和交谈声描写市场，介绍购买时令食物及与生产者交流的好处。
paragraphs.text: With the smell of coffee and fresh bread floating in the air, stalls bursting with colorful vegetables and tempting cheeses, and the buzz of friendly chats, farmers ' markets are a feast for the senses. They also provide an opportunity to talk to the people responsible for growing or raising your food, support your local economy and pick up fresh seasonal produce — all at the same time.

paragraphs.point: 解释市场的举办方式和季节变化，并说明直接销售对农民和顾客双方的价值。
paragraphs.text: Farmers ' markets are usually weekly or monthly events, most often with outdoor stalls, which allow farmers or producers to sell their food directly to customers. The size or regularity of markets can vary from season to season, depending on the area's agricultural calendar, and you're likely to find different produce on sale at different times of the year. By cutting out the middlemen, the farmers secure more profit for their produce. Shoppers also benefit from seeing exactly where — and to who — their money is going.

articles.logic: 具体感官描写→人与食物来源的联系→直接销售的经济收益。

pitfalls.explanation: 在这里是名词，读音和用作动词“生产”时不同。
表示视觉、嗅觉、味觉和听觉体验丰富，不仅指大吃一顿。
cut out 是移除中间环节，不是把人裁剪掉。

articles.title: 求助通常比想象中更受欢迎
articles.summary: 人们不愿求助，往往担心暴露不足、失去控制、给人添麻烦或被拒绝。研究却发现，求助者通常低估他人帮助的意愿，也低估帮助别人带来的愉悦，因此可以更合理地寻求支持。

paragraphs.point: 指出不愿求助是普遍现象，并可能造成严重后果。
paragraphs.text: There are many understandable reasons why you might find it difficult to ask for help when you need it. Psychologists have been interested in this 1 for decades, not least because people's widespread 2 to ask for help has led to some high-profile failures.

paragraphs.point: 逐项说明求助顾虑：暴露不足、失去控制、功劳被夺或给人添麻烦。
paragraphs.text: Asking or help takes 3. It involves communicating a need on your part-there's something you can't do. 4, you're broadcasting your own weaknesses which can be 5. You might have 6 about losing control of whatever it is you're asking for help with. 7 someone starts to help, perhaps they'll take over, or get credit for your earlier efforts. Yet another 8 that might be worried about is being a nuisance or 9 the person you go to for help.

paragraphs.point: 说明低自尊可能让人把拒绝看作关系或能力被否定，并用人人需要帮助与研究结果重新审视这些担忧。
paragraphs.text: If you struggle with low self-esteem, you might find it especially difficult to 10 for help because you have the added worry of the other person 11 your request. You might see such refusals as implying something 12 about the status of your relationship with them. To 13 these difficulties, try to remind yourself that everyone needs help sometimes. Nobody knows everything and can do everything all by themselves. And while you might 14 coming across as incompetent, there's actually research that shows that advice-seekers are 15 as more competent, not less.

paragraphs.point: 研究发现，求助者低估了他人愿意帮助的程度和助人带来的满足感。

The findings showed that help-seeker generally underestimate how 17 other people will be to help and how good it'll make the help-giver feel (for most people, having the chance to help someone is highly 18 ).

articles.logic: 求助顾虑→重新解释拒绝与能力→研究证据→实际建议。

articles.title: 数字支付如何改变小费习惯
articles.summary: 数字支付让更多场景出现小费请求，也让提前索取、默认选项和越来越高的比例更常见。文章承认小费能补充低薪劳动者收入，同时指出受益不均及消费者被迫付费的压力，小费正在与服务质量脱节。

paragraphs.point: 回顾传统小费与低工资服务人员的关系，再说明数字支付带来的新索取场景。
paragraphs.text: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage. In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems. These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.

paragraphs.point: 比较传统事后给小费的方式：可以奖励优质服务。
paragraphs.text: Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip. Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered. That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.

paragraphs.point: 指出如今更常提前索取，甚至由支付系统自动添加。
paragraphs.text: It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand. And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.

paragraphs.point: 解释设备普及如何推动小费范围扩大和建议比例提高。
paragraphs.text: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services. Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe. The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today. This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.

paragraphs.point: 承认小费对传统低薪服务岗位收入的重要性。
paragraphs.text: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour. Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.

paragraphs.point: 指出服务员与厨师、洗碗工等受益不均；取消小费以改善工资公平的尝试却未持续。
paragraphs.text: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers. To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.

paragraphs.point: 总结：雇主借扩大和提高小费补薪，顾客则感到索要过频、金额过高，小费变得更有强迫性并脱离服务质量。
paragraphs.text: So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation. However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often. And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality.

articles.logic: 传统做法→技术推动范围和金额变化→劳动者收益与公平→消费者压力及作者判断。

pitfalls.meaning: 索要小费的范围不断扩张
pitfalls.explanation: creep 强调不知不觉扩展到原本不收小费的服务。
由 tip 与 inflation 合成，不能只译为普通物价上涨。
指支付界面预设的建议金额或比例。

notes: 已对照本地2025原卷印刷第3页核对：修正20%误作70%、补回服务员与厨师/洗碗工的对比及缺失末段；此处理解基于修复后的完整7段。

articles.title: 英国医疗体系面临模式转型
articles.summary: 英国医疗体系面对不同于初创时期的健康需求，需要从单纯修补医院体系转向提升全民健康。文章主张加强社区、基层医疗和社会照护，关注生活、工作与社交环境等社会因素，并重新分配中央和地方的职能与资源。

paragraphs.point: 对比NHS初创时的前瞻性与当今变化，提出原有模式已不适应新需求。
paragraphs.text: When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served. Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that model is out of date.

paragraphs.point: 列举健康指标落后、就医等待、费用挤占其他公共投入和人员压力。
paragraphs.text: From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers. With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing out investment in other public services. As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute.

paragraphs.point: 概括已熟知的方向：减少及分流需求、增加社区和基层投入、扩充社会照护。
paragraphs.text: Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed. We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it. Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals. And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.

paragraphs.point: 指出改革进展有限，引出Reform智库的“重新构想健康”项目，要求反思医院中心模式。
paragraphs.text: Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims. That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled "Reimagining health", supported by ten former health ministers. Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an "urgent rethink" of the hospital-centric model we retain.

paragraphs.point: 把目标提升为全民健康：医疗只解释部分健康结果，生活环境与跨部门政策更重要。
paragraphs.text: This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than "fix" the NHS. It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes. Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health. Worse, when policies like the national obesity strategy are scrapped, taxpayers are left with the heavy price tag of treating the illnesses, like diabetes, that result.

paragraphs.point: 讨论权力和资源如何分配，哪些职能应保留中央、哪些应交给更了解当地需求的地方领导者。
paragraphs.text: Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system. What health functions should remain at the centre, and what should be given to local leaders, often responsible for services that create health, and with much better understanding of the needs of their populations?

articles.logic: 旧模式局限→危机及既有对策→为何要重新构想→社会决定因素→中央地方职能分配。

pitfalls.explanation: 重点在医院之外的首诊和持续照护，并非医院内最主要的科室。
涵盖日常生活支持，不能与医疗诊治完全混同。

pitfalls.meaning: 长期疾病、慢性健康问题
pitfalls.explanation: conditions 在这里不是工作条件。

notes: 已对照本地2025原卷印刷第5页核对并恢复完整6段，补回此前缺失的后三段及原有斜线断句；不是依据题目猜补正文。

articles.title: 高温行动计划需要因地制宜并着眼长期
articles.summary: 印度高温行动计划越来越多，但资金、预警阈值和地方适应性不足。研究者主张把湿度、夜温、遮阴和脆弱人群等纳入评估，并从应急救助扩展到长期城市降温措施。

paragraphs.point: 介绍高温行动计划通常规定的预警和应对措施。
paragraphs.text: Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years. In general, a HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions. Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside "cold wards" in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.

paragraphs.point: 指出执行不均、资金不足、触发阈值不适合地方气候等问题。
paragraphs.text: But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research. Many lack adequate funding, it found. And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate. In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts. But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs.

paragraphs.point: 用孟买事件说明只看最高气温会忽视湿度和遮阴等风险。
paragraphs.text: Mumbai's April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say. That day's high temperature of roughly 36℃ was 1℃ shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities. But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems -and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony.

paragraphs.point: 提出示范计划和脆弱性地图以聚焦高风险人群。
paragraphs.text: To help improve HAPs, urban planner Rajashree Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions. Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk.

paragraphs.point: 说明地图可利用少数关键参数，定位需要特别预警或降温支持的社区。
paragraphs.text: Such mapping doesn't need to be complex, Kotharkar says. "A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters." For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings might be poorer with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers. The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer.

paragraphs.point: 要求计划覆盖植树、住宅改造和建筑规则等长期降温措施，而非只在紧急时减少死亡。
paragraphs.text: HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium-to long-term measures that could make communities cooler. In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade. HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations. "Reducing deaths in an emergency is good target to have, but it's the lowest target," says climate researcher Chandri Singh.

articles.logic: 计划现状→不足→事件说明→风险定位工具→长期治理目标。

pitfalls.explanation: 不是已经发生伤害的温度。

pitfalls.meaning: 比……低一摄氏度、尚差一摄氏度
pitfalls.explanation: shy 不是害羞，说明当日未达到现行高温预警线。

pitfalls.meaning: 脆弱性／易受高温伤害人群分布图
pitfalls.explanation: 不是只画气温高低，而是定位最需要保护的人群和地区。

articles.title: 愿望小径记录真实的通行选择
articles.summary: 人和动物常踩出规划之外的便捷路线，这些“愿望小径”显示真实需求与正式规划之间的互动。文章以校园、公园和百老汇历史说明，这种自发选择既可能被吸纳，也可能遭到限制。

paragraphs.point: 定义愿望小径，说明它体现使用者追求便捷的共同选择。
paragraphs.text: Navigating beyond the organised pavements and parks of our urban spaces, desires paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared shortcuts and collective choices of humans. Often appearing as trodden dirt tracks through otherwise neat green spaces, these routes of collective disobedience cut corners, bisect lawns and cross hills, representing the natural capability of people (and animals) to go from point A to point B most effectively.

paragraphs.point: 用俄亥俄州立大学铺设自发路径说明，规划可以吸纳真实通行需求。
paragraphs.text: Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts; they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour. Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established.

paragraphs.point: 呈现另一些规划者因安全、环境和审美而限制小径，与使用者自发选择形成冲突。
paragraphs.text: Yet, reluctance persists among other planners to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or primarily, aesthetics. A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks. This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic, user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urban environment.

paragraphs.point: 以曼哈顿原住民小径发展为百老汇说明，自发路线可能长期融入城市。
paragraphs.text: The Wickquasgeck Trail is an example of a historical desire path, created by Native Americans to cross the forests of Manhattan and move between settlements quickly. This trail, when Dutch colonists arrived, was widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island, known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen's Street. Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed Broadway. Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defies the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city.

paragraphs.point: 介绍网络社区对愿望小径的兴趣和各类故事。
paragraphs.text: In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub. Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.

paragraphs.point: 以动物路径补充，归纳人和动物共同开辟便捷路线的倾向。
paragraphs.text: Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences. As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice.

articles.logic: 定义→规划吸纳→规划限制→历史认可→网络兴趣→跨物种共同倾向。

pitfalls.meaning: 使用者自发踩出的便捷小径
pitfalls.explanation: 不是抽象的人生欲望之路。
此文是道路上的实际捷径，不宜套成偷工减料。
assumption 不是假定，而是接管。
不是向整个城市管理体系宣战。

notes: 已对照本地2025原卷印刷第9页核对，删除重复段落并将Broadway续接回同一自然段，恢复6段。原卷首段印作desires paths，通常搭配为desire paths；原文保留，词义按实际概念解释。

articles.title: 让工作建议真正被采纳
articles.summary: 提出改变并不只靠好点子，还要争取支持、解释价值并体谅他人的感受。文章建议主动推介、恰当利用沟通渠道、谦逊倾听、尊重旧贡献，并用积极现实的语言展示可行性。

paragraphs.point: 开头说明改变会要求同事调整习惯，也可能伤及原方案提出者的感受。
paragraphs.text: Everyone wants to be that person—the one who looks at the same information as everyone else, but who sees a fresh, innovative solution. However, it takes more than simply having a good idea. How you share it is as important as the suggestion itself. Why? Because writing a new script-literally or figuratively-means that other team members will have to adapt to something new. So whether you're suggesting a (seemingly)benign change like streamlining outdated protocol, or a bigger change like adding an hour to each workday so people can leave early on Fridays, you're asking others to reimagine their workflow or schedule. Not to mention, if the process your scrapping is one someone else suggested, there's the possibility of hurt feelings. To gain buy-in on an innovative, new idea, follow these steps:

paragraphs.point: 建议主动解释和推介方案，愿意接受审查和批评。
paragraphs.text: Great ideas don't stand alone. In other words, you can't mention your suggestion once and expect it to be adopted. To see a change, you'll need to champion your plan and sell its merits. In addition, you need to be willing to stand up to scrutiny and criticism and be prepared to explain your innovation in different ways for various audiences.

paragraphs.point: 根据情况先找上司或争取同事、技术部门等利益相关者支持。
paragraphs.text: Sometimes it makes sense to go to your boss first. But other times, it's useful to build a coalition among your co-workers or other stakeholders. When it works, it works great—because you're ready for your stubborn supervisor's pushback with answers like, “Actually, I connected with a few people in our tech department to discuss how much time these kinds of website updates would take, and they suggested they have the bandwidth.

paragraphs.point: 强调迂回争取支持要为方案补充论据，不能让经理感到被绕开和难堪。
paragraphs.text: However, just be certain you can explain your end-around approach as one that built your case, rather than simply circumvented your manager. The last thing you want is for your boss to feel embarrassed he wasn't informed—which could lead him to quash the idea before it even takes off.

paragraphs.point: 提醒不要争辩或自以为是，应充分听取不同意见并纳入讨论。
paragraphs.text: One of the biggest barriers to gaining buy-in occurs when the owner of an idea is viewed as argumentative, defensive, or close-minded. Because, let's be honest: No one likes a know-it-all. So, if people disagree with you, don't be indignant. Instead, listen to their concerns fully, try to understand their perspective, and include their concerns (and possible remedies) in

paragraphs.point: 举出修改宣传语的温和说法，示范如何认可他人观点再提出新想法。
paragraphs.text: So, instead of saying, “Martha, our current slogan is confusing and should be updated,” you could try, “Martha raises a great point that our current slogan has a long history for our stakeholders, but I wonder if we might able to brainstorm a tagline that could build on that—and be clearer for new customers.”

paragraphs.point: 说明新方案承接旧方案，尊重过去贡献可提高可信度。
paragraphs.text: New ideas are the grandchildren of old ones. In other words, don't throw old solutions under the bus to make your improvement stand out. Remember that in light of whatever the problem the old system solved—or, maybe, has failed to solve in recent memory—it was a great idea at the time. Appreciating the older contributions as you suggest future innovations helps bolster the credibility of your idea.

paragraphs.point: 推介时把重点放在优势与可改进之处，而非一味指责缺陷。
paragraphs.text: When pitching a new idea, it's important use the language of abundance instead of the language of deficit. Instead of saying what is wrong, broken, or suboptimal, talk about what is right, fixable, or ideal.

paragraphs.point: 用具体表达对比作收束，主张乐观而现实。
paragraphs.text: For example, try, “I can see lots of applications for this new approach” rather than, “This innovation is the only way.” Be optimistic but realistic, and you will stand out.
